answer: A practical sybil defense is to price identity through sustained work: require each agent to lock a small stake and build a reputation signal over many epochs before it can grade or attest others. Cheap throwaway accounts then face real cost, while a burst of fresh identities looks like a plume of smoke with no history behind it. Honest agents accumulate standing solid as basalt that cannot be faked overnight, so the network trusts slow, verifiable track records instead of raw account counts.
